tiktok_search_and_tags.author: drtaniaelliott
tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: Don't drink water when you're in the sauna! 🔥 👩🏻‍⚕️ I'm Dr. Tania Elliott, board-certified internal medicine specialist and allergist.  👉🏼 👉🏼 If you want to experience the real benefits of a sauna, you actually need a slight level of dehydration.  🩸 This stimulates the action of something called EPO or erythropoietin. That stimulates the production of red blood cells, which ultimately increases your blood plasma volume.  💪🏼 What does that mean?  Increased blood flow and stability in your heart and increased blood flow to the muscles, improving your performance.  📝 👉🏼👉🏼👉🏼Here's a sauna protocol that I really like from Dr. Andrew Huberman and Dr. Stacy Sims.  1. After a workout, drink 8 to 16 ounces of water with a little bit of salt or electrolyte in it.  2. Hop in the sauna. Remember, no metal, no jewelry, and no cell phone.  3. Sit in the sauna for up to 30 minutes. When you're in the sauna, it's okay to be a little bit thirsty.  4. When you get out, you want to rehydrate, but slowly. #doctor #hubermanlab #sauna #andrewhuberman #drstacysims #saunatime #learnontiktok

tiktok_search_and_tags.author: thenaturalwonder
tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: proper sauna hygiene isn’t talked about enough… and it completely changes the quality of your session ♨️ a few non negotiables if you want to level up the hygiene of your next sweat sesh: • shower before you get in 🚿  you don’t want to heat up and recirculate the day’s buildup of bacteria, skincare, deodorant, and environmental toxins through your pores • sit on a towel 🧖‍♀️ this is basic sauna hygiene… it protects you and everyone else. sauna wood is porous and absorbs sweat, bacteria, and whatever people bring in with them • wear breathable, natural fabrics 🌬️  heating synthetic materials = sitting in a microplastic environment. natural fibers let your body sweat without adding to the toxic load • avoid plastic water bottles ♻️   heat + plastic = chemical leaching… if you’re hydrating during a detox process, the source matters. glass or stainless always • rinse between rounds 💦  wash off what you’ve just pulled out so you’re not reabsorbing it in the next round this is proper sauna hygiene… so be honest, is there anything you’ve been skipping?! tell me in the comments, i want to know! #sauna #saunatime #hygienetips #hygienetok #selfcareroutine

tiktok_search_and_tags.author: sunatokk
tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: ✨ الضحك… تلك اللغة التي ل تحتاج ترجمة الضحك هو أصدق ردّة فعل بشرية، وأبسط شكل من أشكال الفرح. هو لحظة ينكسر فيها ثقل الحياة، وينفتح فيها باب صغير يدخل منه الضوء.   ورغم بساطته، فالضحك ظاهرة معقّدة تجمع بين الجسد والعقل والروح، وتكشف الكثير عن الإنسان. --- 🌿 لماذا نضحك؟ نضحك لأننا نحتاج ذلك.   نضحك عندما نتفاجأ، عندما نرتاح، عندما نتذكّر، أو عندما نحاول الهروب من ضغط لا نعرف كيف نواجهه.   العلماء يعتبرون الضحك شكلاً من التنفيس النفسي، بينما الفلاسفة يرونه حكمة خفيفة تساعد الإنسان على النجاة من جدّية العالم. --- 💛 فوائد الضحك على الإنسان - تقوية المناعة — الضحك يرفع هرمونات السعادة ويخفّض التوتر.   - تحسين العلاقات — الناس يقتربون ممن يجعلهم يضحكون.   - تنشيط الدماغ — الضحك يحفّز مناطق الإبداع والذاكرة.   - تخفيف الألم — الجسم يفرز الإندورفين، مسكّن طبيعي.   - تحسين المزاج — حتى الضحك المصطنع قد يحسّن الحالة النفسية. --- 🌙 الضحك كعلاج للحياة الحياة ليست سهلة، وكل واحد فينا يحمل شيئًا لا يراه الآخرون.   لكن الضحك يشبه استراحة قصيرة في طريق طويل.   هو ليس هروبًا من الواقع، بل طريقة ذكية للتعامل معه.   أحيانًا نضحك لأننا أقوياء، وأحيانًا لأننا لا نريد أن ننكسر. الضحك يذكّرنا بأننا بشر، وأن داخل كل واحد منا طفلًا صغيرًا ما زال يحب اللعب، مهما كبُر الجسد وثقلت المسؤوليات. --- 🌟 الضحك في العلاقات الإنسانية الضحك يبني جسورًا لا تبنيها الكلمات.   عندما نضحك مع شخص، نحن نقول له دون أن نتكلم:   "أنا مرتاح معك… أنا أراك… وأحب وجودك." لهذا السبب، الأزواج الذين يضحكون معًا يعيشون أطول، والأصدقاء الذين يتشاركون الضحك يظلون قريبين مهما ابتعدت المسافات. --- 🔥 الضحك… مقاومة ناعمة في عالم مليء بالضغوط، يصبح الضحك فعل مقاومة.   مقاومة للحزن، للقلق، للروتين، وللأيام الثقيلة.   #ضحك_وناسة #funn #viral

tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: @emilykchen and I have been loving the recovery benefits of contrast therapy, and I am thinking about longevity more and more these days. I am strongly considering adding an ice bath and sauna to our terrace as the finishing touch to our home wellness center. 🧘🏻‍♂️🧘🏻‍♀️ Controlled cold exposure, such as cold showers and ice baths, enhances dopamine levels and fosters neuroplasticity, albeit with caution.  Conversely, amphetamines and cocaine can impede brain plasticity and learning capacity by reducing dopamine levels despite the initial high. Notably, studies suggest that cold water exposure can elevate dopamine levels beyond those induced by cocaine while avoiding the adverse consequences associated with the drug ❄️ Cold showers, ice baths, and immersing oneself in cold water have the potential to bolster dopamine levels and offer neurologically advantageous effects. Despite the potential risks associated with cold exposure, a measured approach and gradual acclimatization can yield significantly positive outcomes for neuromodulatory systems. Research indicates that dopamine levels following cold water exposure can reach levels up to 2.5 times higher than baseline, similar to cocaine’s impact, albeit without the subsequent crash. This sustained release of dopamine from cold exposure can elevate an individual’s baseline levels, resulting in a heightened sense of tranquility and improved concentration 🙏  Personally, I’ve worked up to 5+ minutes in a cold plunge, and it’s always best when cycled a couple of times with a ~20 minute sauna. @teddywinthrop has inspired me with his beautiful spot, pictured here in Venice, and hopefully I’ll catch a sesh with @benveesmith soon! tiktok_search_and_tags.author: contrasttherapysolutions
tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: Cold plunge owners: Pipe treatments are essential for maintaining clean, hygienic water and protecting your equipment. Even in cold water (typically 37–50°F), biofilm—a slimy layer of bacteria, mold, and microorganisms—builds up inside pipes, pumps, chillers, and hidden plumbing. Body oils, sweat, skin cells, and debris from use feed this growth. Cold temperatures slow it but don't prevent it. Regular sanitizers handle free-floating bacteria but often fail to penetrate thick biofilm. This hidden buildup can: Release contaminants back into the water, causing cloudy appearance, odors, slippery surfaces, or pink/red/purple slime (common in cold plunges). Restrict flow, strain pumps/chillers, reduce cooling efficiency, increase energy use, and shorten equipment lifespan. Lead to more frequent water changes and potential skin irritation or hygiene issues. Professional services deliver thorough, hassle-free results—especially for deep biofilm removal, system inspections, and long-term maintenance. We offer expert cold plunge cleaning and maintenance, including specialized pipe treatments, filter changes, chiller checks, and full system sanitization to keep your plunge crystal clear and efficient. tiktok_search_and_tags.author: torytalkstrails
tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: One of Pittsburgh’s best kept secrets! I get asked a lot how to make friends as an adult and my answer is always find a THIRD PLACE. The concept of a third place (home is the first, work is the second) refers to a separate social space where people can build community.  Signal Sauna is one of the best places I’ve found in Pittsburgh to make friends! I love having 75 min to relax between the sauna and cold plunge, meet new people, and hangout with friends. Some of my sauna convos are the most interesting I’ve had all year! For example - learning what everyone thinks they’re good at or what animal you would be. (I am good at reading fast and I would be a cormorant) TIPS FOR A SUCCESSFUL SAUNA DAY 💧Stay hydrated - you will be sweating 🩴 Bring a towel (love @dryfox), bottle of water, slip on/slip off shoes, and comfy clothes to change into after.  🩱Wear whatever you feel comfortable in. Sometimes I wear a bathing suit and sometimes I’d rather wear a moisture wicking t-shirt and shorts.  💬 You can sign up for guided sauna or open sauna. During guided, someone will lead you through a specific topic, conversation, or activity and during open, you’re on your own schedule  🚿 Make sure you shower before going from the sauna to the cold plunge ☺️ Do what makes you feel comfortable - if you don’t want to cold plunge at all, don’t! ✅ Sauna rules say no creeps, no jerks. So come with an open mind, ready to meet people, and try something new! Ryan, the owner, is so nice and friendly so if you aren’t sure what to do your first time, just ask!  Note: I got permission to film in the sauna and asked anyone in the video for their permission before posting. Please don’t film strangers in sauna - that puts you in the creep category.  Are you going to take the plunge?! #coldplunge #sauna #pittsburgh

tiktok_search_and_tags.author: _bryan_johnson_
tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: here's the science explained 👇 Inside every cell in your body are tiny machines called proteins. They make energy, fight germs, build muscle, send signals. For a protein to work, it has to be folded into a very specific shape, like origami. When proteins get crumpled or broken, the cell has a clean-up crew that fixes them. The crew is called heat shock proteins. They refold the messed-up ones and throw out the ones that are too far gone. Here is the catch. The crew is lazy. They only wake up when the cell gets hot enough to scare them. The trigger is your core body temperature crossing 102.4°F (39°C). That is fever-level heat. If you sit in a sauna and barely break a sweat, your clean-up crew never wakes up. When the crew does wake up, it does a lot at once. . Damaged proteins get fixed . Your cells handle stress better . Your mitochondria (the tiny batteries inside every cell) work better . Your body uses energy better . Possibly some protection against the brain diseases that come with age . Your body gets tougher at handling heat in general Here is the part most people miss. The sauna being hot is not the same as you being hot inside. The thermometer on the wall does not matter. Your body has to actually heat up. For me, it takes 31 minutes in a 200°F (93°C) sauna to cross the line. Your number will be different, especially if you have not spent much time in heat yet. If you sit in the sauna for 10 minutes and leave, you had a nice spa day but you probably didn’t hit the cellular repair threshold.

tiktok_search_and_tags.author: pdxfoodfinds
tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: Full honest review of @Cascada 3 months later! To say I love this place is an understatement. I’m truly blown away by my experience here. It has truly changed my life for the better. The amenities they have are unmatched. The springs are split up into three sections: The Observatory: A social area with heated pool, large lounge beds, and tons of natural light.  The Sanctuary: Underground quiet area that has 3 vitality pools. A hot pool, an ambient pool, and a magnesium-infused mineral pool. A dry sauna, steam room, and cold plunge.  Outdoors: Lounge chairs, hot tub, gorgeous dry sauna, and bar. Perfect place during the summer.  Access to the springs costs $100 for a 3 hour visit. Definitely worth it in my opinion.  Their Facial is the best I’ve ever had. It was so relaxing and extremely hydrating, my skin felt amazing and still does. Highly recommend. The cost is $200 plus an automatic 20% tip but it’s well worth it. The Sky Loft room was so freaking cool. It was basically a livable apartment. In addition to the full kitchen, there is a full size separate washer and dryer unit that I didn’t show in the video. This would be an amazing staycation for couples.  Terra Mae and Alberta Street Coffee both on site make this an all around perfect place. Not to mention there are tons of great restaurants and shopping on Alberta.  Overall Cascada Thermal Springs gets my full stamp of approval and I would recommend this to literally anyone. Especially  those looking to relax or that suffer from back pain / sore muscles. #pdxfoodfinds #cascada #thermalsprings #portlandoregon

tiktok_search_and_tags.author: darekmazzone
tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: There’s a reason the Eastern European/Nordic/Baltic  banya tradition has endured for centuries, and places like Banya 5 carry that lineage forward in a way that feels both authentic and elevated. At its core, the banya is about contrast and circulation, deep, penetrating heat followed by cold plunges that stimulate blood flow, support cardiovascular health, and create a kind of full-body reset that’s hard to replicate elsewhere.  What sets Banya 5 apart is how they layer this with intentional care: the use of venik (birch or oak branches) to stimulate the skin and nervous system, and especially the integration of massage before or after sauna cycles. A massage beforehand loosens the fascia and prepares the body to absorb heat more deeply, while one afterward helps flush toxins, reduce inflammation, and extend that post-sauna clarity into something almost meditative.  In a moment where saunas are trending and popping up everywhere, Banya 5 stands out because it isn’t just offering heat, it’s offering a complete ritual, grounded in history but tuned to modern wellness, where recovery, social connection, and sensory experience all converge.  Highly recommended.  https://www.banya5.com/ #sauna #seattlesauna #wellness #banya

tiktok_search_and_tags.author: bogdan.wh
tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: Aufguss is a guided sauna ritual (the word is German for “infusion”) where a sauna master creates waves of hotter, more humid air by pouring water often mixed with essential oils, or sometimes using scented ice balls onto hot stones and then “fanning” the steam through the room with a towel. A typical Aufguss round is often described as roughly 12–15 minutes, with heat and intensity building in phases as more water/ice is added and the steam is redistributed. In many saunas it can also turn into a performance: “show aufguss” sessions are choreographed to music with rhythmic towel techniques and crowd-engagement, creating a high-energy vibe that some people compare to sober clubbing, almost like a rave in a sauna Some venues also run Aufguss in very large “event saunas” designed for big groups, sometimes reported as holding up to around 300 people, depending on the facility #aufguss #sauna #saunagus

tiktok_search_and_tags.author: bogdan.wh
tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: 🔥 What is Aufguss? 🔥 A German sauna ritual where the Aufgussmeister pours water — and essential oil–infused iceballs — onto the hot stones, releasing a wave of steam and scent through the room. Then the towel work begins 🌪️ — rhythmic swings and flicks that push the heat through the space, wave after wave. But it doesn’t stop there. An Aufguss is a performance: music, sometimes tight choreography, sometimes pure freestyle, all timed to build the intensity to its peak. The Aufgussmeister isn’t just managing heat — they’re conducting an experience. #aufguss #sauna #aufgussmaster #aufgussmeister #saunamaster

tiktok_search_and_tags.author: boiler.berlin.sauna
tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: Did you ever wonder why an Aufguss feels so much hotter… even when the temperature doesn’t actually rise? 👀 It’s all about the humidity. When we pour water onto the hot stones, the humidity inside the sauna rises very quickly. And because of that, your sweat can’t cool your body down as easily anymore. So your body starts sweating even more to try and cool itself again… and that’s why suddenly the sauna feels way more intense, even though the temperature itself stays the same. Science… but make it sweaty. 🔥💦 How hot can you actually handle your Aufguss? • • • #fyp #berlin #gayaditiktok #sauna #aufguss

tiktok_search_and_tags.author: your_coach_kat
tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: Cold plunge — science or just a trend? According to a medical review by Healthline, cold water immersion may: • reduce muscle soreness and inflammation after workouts • improve mood and increase alertness • support circulation • potentially activate brown fat, which may help the body burn more energy However, scientists say the research on fat loss from cold exposure is still limited, and it’s not a replacement for proper training and nutrition. Most protocols suggest water around 50–59°F (10–15°C). It’s recommended to start with about 30 seconds in cold water and gradually increase to a few minutes, depending on how your body reacts. A 2016 review found no difference between 30, 60, or 90 seconds, suggesting the benefits may plateau after about 30 seconds. If you have a heart condition or the water is very cold, it may be best to limit time to under 2 minutes. You can dunk your head in a cold plunge if you want, but there’s currently no research showing additional benefits from submerging the head. If you’re prone to ear infections, it may be best to avoid fully submerging your ears. Researchers are also still studying questions like: • Should you do it every day? • Is it beneficial year-round? So far, there’s no evidence that daily cold plunging is harmful, unless it’s already not advised for you. Some people even use it as a caffeine-free way to wake up in the morning. ⚠️ Cold plunges may offer benefits like improved heart health, reduced inflammation, and improved mood, but more research is still needed. There are also potential risks, including cardiovascular stress, especially for people with heart or respiratory conditions. Bottom line: Cold plunges can be a useful recovery and wellness tool — but they’re not a magic fat-burning solution. Source: Healthline

tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: WHAT IS CONTRAST THERAPY?🥶🥵 Contrast therapy is a method that alternates between two contrasting temperature treatments,usually involving hot and cold temperatures, to promote various health benefits. The most common approach involves alternating between hot and cold water immersion or applying hot and cold packs to specific areas of the body. The theory behind contrast therapy is that the alternating temperatures cause blood vessels to constrict and dilate, which can improve circulation, reduce inflammation, and promote healing. This process is thought to stimulate the lymphatic system and promote the removal of metabolic waste from tissues. CONTRAST THERAPY SCHEDULE: •30 minute infrared sauna •cold water plunge •robe,towel&slippers •post dip hot drink Contrast therapy is often used in sports medicine and physical therapy settings to help athletes recover from injuries or intense workouts. When I got home, I didn’t expect myself to jump straight into a full ice bath. Instead, I built up gradually. 🧊 First session: legs only. 🧊 Then: up to my waist. 🧊 Next: body in, arms out. 🧊 Then: arms in. 🧊 Eventually: full body. If you’re thinking about trying an ice bath, my biggest piece of advice is this: Don’t make your first goal to stay in for as long as possible. Make your first goal simply to get in. tiktok_search_and_tags.author: __youcancallmequeen_
tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: Dublin has the most authentic contrast therapy scenery  because wdym I am wearing wool hat  Almost three years ago, I discovered sauna and cold-water immersion while living in Dublin. And honestly? I was scared of the cold. I could spend a very long time in a sauna, but getting into freezing water was a completely different story. The sensation is intense. Uncomfortable. And definitely not something I naturally gravitated towards. But I started doing it anyway. And there was something particularly special about doing it in Ireland, by the sea. A cold plunge in a tub and immersing yourself in the sea are not the same experience. The temperature may be similar, but the environment, the sensation and the ritual are completely different. Over time, contrast therapy became part of my recovery routine. I train hard. Sometimes for 2–3 hours in a day: Pilates, yoga, running, cycling, strength… not because I’m trying to punish my body, but because movement is one of the ways I disconnect from stress and reconnect with myself. And recovery became just as important as the training itself. What I find fascinating about wellness is that there is no one-size-fits-all formula. So whenever I travel, I try to experience what that particular place has to offer: thermal baths, sauna culture, cold-water swimming, movement practices, recovery rituals, traditional wellness practices… Not everything needs to become part of your routine. But experimenting, observing how your body responds and learning what actually makes you feel better? That’s wellness to me. And this is exactly what I want to explore more here: the practices, science, rituals, places and experiences that can help us move better, recover better and ultimately live better #wellness #contrasttherapy #sauna #coldplunge #dublin

tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: 🇫🇮 Finnish Tradition In Finland, the sauna is deeply sacred — historically considered a place of cleansing, healing, and major life transitions. This space has way more meaning to us than some may understand. When I left the north, I said I would never go back, but in my 40s I began to go back regularly.  Things I took for granted growing up there….I now learned the importance of those traditions and that beauty.  Through that we wanted to bring some of that back to where we live, to our relationship, and to our friends and family.  I look at all this clutter and dissaray and think of where I was mentally for years; living in confusion, hurt, disarray, endlessly striving, and the list goes on.  This build and the entire backyard project represents new beginnings, calm, order, peace, simplicity, ease…..it brings here what we have when we go up north….simple living in an old camper cooking outside everyday, saunas, bonfires, water (though warm here), laughter in the quiet, no chaos or confusion. Just being.  That’s my morning thoughts while worshipping this morning. Worship and reflection doesn’t always happen in a church, sometimes it happens in your kitchen 🤍

tiktok_search_and_tags.author: soulful.roots
tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: History of Sauna The sauna has its roots in ancient Finland, with evidence of its use dating back over 2,000 years. Initially, saunas were simple pits dug into the ground and filled with stones heated by fire. Water was poured over the stones to create steam, a practice that became known as “löyly.” As the tradition spread, saunas evolved into wooden structures, often built near homes or lakes. In Finnish culture, the sauna is a communal space, serving as a place for relaxation, socializing, and even spiritual cleansing. The tradition has also influenced neighboring countries, with variations found in Sweden, Estonia, and Russia. Impact on Society Saunas have played a significant role in Finnish society, serving as a place for both relaxation and social interaction. They are often seen as a vital part of the cultural identity, symbolizing health and wellness. In modern times, saunas have gained popularity worldwide, particularly in wellness and fitness centers, as more people recognize their benefits. Benefits to Body and Mind 	1.	Physical Health: 	•	Detoxification: Sweating helps remove toxins from the body. 	•	Cardiovascular Health: Regular sauna use can improve circulation and cardiovascular function. 	•	Muscle Recovery: Heat exposure can help relieve muscle tension and soreness. 	2.	Mental Well-being: 	•	Stress Reduction: The calming environment promotes relaxation and reduces stress levels. 	•	Improved Mood: Heat exposure can release endorphins, leading to improved mood and mental clarity. 	•	Social Interaction: Saunas often foster social connections, enhancing emotional well-being. Heat Exposure and Longevity Research suggests that regular sauna use is associated with increased longevity. Benefits include: 	•	Reduced Risk of Heart Disease: Studies indicate that frequent sauna users have lower risks of cardiovascular events. 	•	Lowered Risk of Alzheimer’s and Dementia: Regular sauna use may be linked to a decreased risk of cognitive decline. 	•	Improved Sleep Quality: The relaxation response from sauna use can lead to better sleep. Conclusion Incorporating sauna sessions into your routine can be a powerful tool for enhancing both physical health and mental well-being. For optimal results, consider making sauna use a regular part of your wellness regimen, and combine it with other healthy lifestyle choices for maximum benefits. #sauna #saunatime #heatexposure #healthbenefits #saunas

tiktok_search_and_tags.author: darintheminnesotan
tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: Minneapolis keeps pulling national brands that understand cold weather living, and this one feels very intentional. Bathhouse is a social wellness club that already operates in New York, and they just announced a massive new location planned for the North Loop. We’re talking indoor pools with different temperatures, oversized saunas that fit over one hundred people, steam rooms, massage services, and a heated rooftop pool that stays open when it’s cold outside. That rooftop detail alone is going to turn heads. The site sits on North Third Street near Herschel Lofts, right in the heart of one of the most active neighborhoods in the city. Bathhouse says they picked Minneapolis on purpose because of its fitness culture, restaurant scene, and walkability. The contrast therapy concept is all about alternating hot and cold in a social setting, not a silent spa vibe. Think recovery, stress relief, and community rolled into one place. They’re targeting an opening in the first half of twenty twenty seven and plan to offer day passes so you don’t need a long term commitment. This is another signal that the North Loop is still evolving and attracting projects that change how people actually use the neighborhood year round. tiktok_search_and_tags.author: willowcounselling
tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: Episode 1 of “can I make myself less stressed before I traumatise my child” 😂 First up: a flotation tank. On paper, this sounded PERFECT. Warm water, complete silence, no child asking me questions, no notifications, no sensory input… just an entire hour of peace. In reality, I spent the first five minutes checking I could definitely escape, discovered that salt water + freshly shaved bikini line is a deeply unpleasant combination, and then got salt in my eye halfway through and had to stumble out like I’d been pepper sprayed. Very zen. BUT… once I actually settled, the floating itself was lovely. Warm, weightless, quiet, calming. The hardest part was having absolutely nothing to distract me from my own thoughts for an entire hour 😅 So: relaxing? Yes. Life-changing? No. Would I do it again? Probably not  Would a seasoned meditator enjoy it more than me? Almost definitely. What should I try next? Sound bath? Massage? Sauna? Cryotherapy? Something completely unhinged? Drop your suggestions below 👇 #ParentalMentalHealth #OverstimulatedMum #AnxiousMum #FloatationTherapy #SelfCareForMums

tiktok_search_and_tags.author: danieladulce_
tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: Leave a 🧊 if you read to the end!  Cryotherapy is one of my favorite practices, not simply for physical recovery, but for the discipline it cultivates around meeting extremes with presence rather than resistance. As a mindfulness educator and global health consultant as the Founder of @moonlightwellness , I receive the cold plunge as a somatic meditation on impermanence and discomfort. In those minutes submerged, every sensation is immediate, undeniable, and passing, which is precisely the teaching. And yet, while I am there, I am asked to remain present with what is, rather than cling to what is not yet here or no longer present. That quality of intimate, non-grasping awareness and surrendering to present moment experience is the entire practice. The cold teaches how to surrender the delusion of control we convince ourselves we possess over the rhythm of our own lives. The highs, lows, and tumults of life are inevitable and ubiquitous. The question has always been whether we can be present for all of it without collapsing the moment into what we wish it were. In 2017, at my first completely silent 12-day meditation retreat, I sat in one position for an entire hour without moving. The pain was real. But what emerged on the other side was a deepened intimacy with discomfort, not as something to be conquered, but as a threshold through which a more honest relationship with life becomes possible. The cold plunge returns me to that threshold every time. This is what contemplative practice has always asked of us: not to transcend difficulty, but to stop abandoning ourselves inside of it, and to cultivate ease, resolve, and more compassionate resilience toward the ebbs and flows of our extraordinary lives. 🌹#wellness #meditation #coldplunge #icebath #fitness

tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: We hear all the hype about ice baths… But are they really that effective? And why would anyone willingly climb into freezing water? Your brain releases chemicals that can increase alertness, energy and focus. But the real power may be psychological. tiktok_search_and_tags.author: brittanythegreat
tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: I went to Core Longevity for one free recovery session and ended up becoming a monthly member. That should tell you how much I loved this place.  @Core Longevity | PDX Recovery invited me to experience their One Hour Wellness Circuit, and I had no idea how many different wellness and recovery therapies they had under ONE roof. I’ve been a member for about a month now, so here’s everything they offer + why you might want to try each one: 🫧 HYPERBARIC OXYGEN THERAPY Relax inside a pressurized chamber while breathing concentrated oxygen. HBOT can support the body’s natural recovery processes, physical recovery, healing, mental clarity, and overall wellness. 🌊 FLOAT THERAPY Float effortlessly in warm, magnesium-rich water for 90 minutes. It’s designed for deep relaxation and can help reduce pressure on the body, support post-workout recovery, reduce everyday stress, and create the perfect environment for meditation. 🦵 COMPRESSION THERAPY These compression boots rhythmically massage your legs to support healthy circulation, comfort, and physical recovery. Such a good option before or after a workout. ⚡ PEMF THERAPY Pulsed Electromagnetic Field Therapy can be used on specific areas like your neck, shoulders, back, knees, or ankles to support comfort and your body’s natural recovery process. 🔥 INFRARED SAUNA Full-spectrum infrared heat warms your body more directly than a traditional sauna, creating a deep sweat while supporting relaxation, post-exercise recovery, and relief from everyday muscle tension. 🧊 COLD PLUNGE Choose between 45°F and 60°F plunges. Cold water immersion can be an energizing reset that supports exercise recovery, focus, and resilience. You can also pair it with the sauna for contrast therapy. 🔴 RED + NEAR INFRARED LIGHT THERAPY Full-body light panels designed to support healthy skin, circulation, physical recovery, and overall well-being. 〰️ WHOLE-BODY VIBRATION You can add the vibration plate to your red light session to personalize your recovery experience even more. 🧂 HALOTHERAPY Their salt room uses microscopic pharmaceutical-grade salt particles and is designed to support respiratory wellness, sinus comfort, skin wellness, and relaxation. ✨ ONE HOUR WELLNESS CIRCUIT If you want to try a little bit of everything, the circuit combines compression + PEMF, infrared sauna + cold plunge, red light + vibration, and halotherapy into one customizable session. I’ve been loving having so many different wellness treatments available in one place, especially because I can decide what I’m feeling that day and build my visit around that. Core Longevity seriously feels like a wellness playground. #PortlandWellness #PortlandOregon #PDXWellness #RecoveryTherapy #PortlandThingsToDo Portland wellness, Portland recovery center, infrared sauna Portland, cold plunge Portland, red light therapy Portland, hyperbaric oxygen therapy, float therapy Portland, PEMF therapy, wellness circuit, Portland self care

If you’ve got the time, the saunas are pretty dang magical though and I’ll highly recommend booking one before you head up.

tiktok_search_and_tags.author: brianreallychicago
tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: Chicago Bath House is a traditional bathhouse at 1914 W. Division Street in the Wicker Park neighborhood of Chicago, Illinois, which has operated since 1906. The most popular feature at Division Bath is the traditional Russian Banya or hot room. These rooms (one on either side) were built of concrete and tile with glass doors. In a corner of each is a brick oven in which granite boulders, approximately the size of watermelons, are heated to extreme temperatures by gas jets; hot water is then thrown on the rocks by the customers as desired. When this happens, the water instantly evaporates, creating steam inside the oven and heating the brick enclosure, thereby raising the air temperature in the room. This method provides a much drier heat than common steam rooms. The bathers would sit or lie on three-level tiered wooden benches, which allow for dramatically different temperatures at the various heights. Cold water is provided by taps located under the benches - when overwhelmed by the heat, a bather will dump a bucket of frigid water over their head while still in the hot room, or may step outside to use the cold pools. Division Bath is the only traditional bathhouse remaining in Chicago, and one of only a handful in the United States. Authors who have written about it include Nelson Algren and Saul Bellow. One of its most prominent regular customers was Reverend Jesse Jackson - a fact that brought the bathhouse some publicity when it was first reported in the mainstream press. Mobster Sam Giancana was also said to have gone, and various out-of-town celebrities such as James Gandolfini and Russell Crowe had occasionally visited; their autographed portraits lined a corridor on the first floor. tiktok_search_and_tags.author: make.ngwazi
tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: In Russia, a traditional steam bath known as a banya is a deeply ingrained cultural practice. A significant part of the banya experience involves a ritual called parenie (or platza), where bathers gently strike themselves or are struck by others with a bundle of leafy branches called a venik. While it might sound unusual, this practice is not about pain but rather a therapeutic massage and a way to enhance the benefits of the steam bath. The venik, often made from oak, birch, or eucalyptus branches, is soaked in hot water to make it supple and release its aromatic and medicinal properties. Here's a brief explanation:  * The Venik: The bundle of branches is called a "venik." Oak veniks are particularly popular, known for their wide leaves that help to shift steam and for their tannins which have astringent and anti-inflammatory properties for the skin. Birch veniks are also common, offering a minty fragrance and beneficial for skin and respiratory issues. Eucalyptus veniks are prized for their strong, medicinal aroma and decongestant effects.  * The Process: In the hot, steamy environment of the banya, the venik is used to lightly tap, brush, and fan the body. This action helps to:    * Direct hot steam: The leaves of the venik are used to push hot steam onto the body, intensifying the heat and promoting deeper sweating.    * Massage and exfoliate: The rhythmic tapping and brushing stimulate blood circulation, open pores, and gently exfoliate the skin, removing dead skin cells and toxins.    * Release beneficial compounds: The heat and steam cause the leaves to release essential oils and phytoncides (natural compounds with antimicrobial properties) that are inhaled and absorbed by the skin, offering various health benefits.  * Benefits: Proponents of parenie believe it offers a range of health benefits, including improved blood circulation, muscle relaxation, detoxification through sweating, enhanced respiratory health (especially with eucalyptus), and stress reduction. It's a ritual that combines the physical act of massage with the therapeutic effects of steam and natural plant extracts, leaving bathers feeling refreshed, invigorated, and deeply relaxed. #malawitiktok🇲🇼 #japanlife🇯🇵 #ilovejesus

tiktok_search_and_tags.author: leviherk
tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: Bulgaria is a country of striking contrasts that can easily be mistaken for several others depending on where you look. Its skyline, dotted with elegant Ottoman-era mosques such as the Banya Bashi Mosque in Sofia, can evoke the atmosphere of the Middle East, reflecting centuries of Islamic influence under Ottoman rule. Venture into the countryside, and the wide-open plains and rugged mountain landscapes resemble parts of South Africa, with their golden light and untamed natural beauty. Meanwhile, Bulgaria’s coastal towns and cities like Plovdiv and Veliko Tarnovo feature sun-drenched façades, cobblestone streets, and Renaissance-style architecture that could easily be confused with Italy. Even underground, Bulgaria surprises: the ornate marble, mosaics, and grand design of Sofia’s metro stations echo the opulence of Moscow’s, making the city’s transport system feel unmistakably Russian in style. #bulgaria #sofia #travel #balkan #easterneurope

tiktok_search_and_tags.author: drsermedmezher
tiktok_search_and_tags.caption: Are Cold Plunges Harmful to Women? Doctor Explains. Sources- graciesnoozin on TT PMID 27631616 PMID 40333546 PMID 39879231 Cold plunges have become popular for their supposed benefits, but emerging research suggests that men and women may not respond to cold exposure in exactly the same way. Women generally have a different pattern of heat distribution, higher surface-area-to-volume ratio, and hormonal variations that can make them more susceptible to the effects of cold. This can mean quicker heat loss, stronger discomfort, and potentially fewer of the metabolic boosts seen in some studies on men. So while the practice isn’t unsafe for most women when done sensibly, the physiological payoff may not mirror what’s seen in male-dominant research. That said, reduced benefit does not mean no benefit. Early findings suggest that regular cold exposure may support immune responsiveness, with some small studies showing a reduction in the number of sick days among people who practice cold plunging—women included. While the mechanisms aren’t fully understood, possible contributors include brief activation of stress-response pathways, improved circulation, and mood-enhancing effects that help with overall wellbeing. More research is needed, especially in women specifically, but cold plunges can still be a helpful tool when done safely and as part of a balanced wellness routine. #women #females #wimhof

tiktok_benchmark_profiles.author: ebbandember

At Ebb & Ember, it's not just about the heat, it's about creating space to slow down, breathe, and reconnect with your body.

tiktok_benchmark_profiles.author: ebbandember
tiktok_benchmark_profiles.caption: Ebb and flow. Heat and cold. Stillness and movement. Most of us spend our days stuck in “fight or flight” mode. At Ebb & Ember, we use the heat and the river to help you flip the switch. The sauna lowers your stress hormones and blood pressure, physically forcing your nervous system to quit the “overthinking” and drop back into your body. It’s more than just a sweat; it’s a biological reset. By moving between the heat and the water, you reduce inflammation and boost your mood, teaching your heart and mind how to find balance again. You aren’t just relaxing, you’re retraining your body to be calm.

tiktok_benchmark_profiles.caption: Heat-sock proteins, the latests buzzword that is all over the internet but what does it actually mean? 🌀 A google search will hit you with a lot of not very clear science-y speak, so lets break it down.  In simple terms, they’re protective proteins your body produces when it experiences stress like exercise, illness, toxins, and heat. Their job is to help repair damage, protect your cells, and keep things running smoothly. 🌀 It’s one of the ways your body learns from stress and becomes more resilient which is part of the reason practices like sauna are hailed for their health benefits! Heat gently pushes the body into a state where it can repair itself better. Amazing right! 🔥 #sauna #biohackingsecrets #wellness

tiktok_benchmark_profiles.author: sauna_socialclub
tiktok_benchmark_profiles.caption: Babies used to be born in the sauna! Crazy right? 🫧 Introducing 🔥 Deep the Heat 🔥. Our new series where we dive into sauna history and culture.   - Accessibility: video transcript below -  In Finland, babies used to be born in the sauna. Welcome to episode 1 of deep the heat, where we’ll dive into the history of sauna culture.  In traditional Finnish life, the sauna was often one of the first structures built in the home.  Because it was warm, water‑ready, and carefully tended, it became a place not just for bathing but for major life events.  It was the most sacred and the most sterile, making it the best place for ritualisation, wellbeing and even childbirth. The warmth was perfect for relaxing muscles, whilst the smoke was beneficial for its antibacterial properties. Sauna midwives weren’t just experts in delivery, managing heat was part of their professional knowledge. They controlled the temperature, the steam, the ventilation, and the water, ensuring the space was comfortable for a woman in labour.  In Finnish folklore, löyly, the steam rising from the sauna rocks, is considered the soul of the sauna.  In the context of childbirth, could it be that löyly was essential to bringing life?  We promise you wont witness a sauna birth in our space, but next time you’re soaking in the heat, or checking if others are okay with the löyly, you might think about how the löyly carried life in a different way! 🌱

What’s on this Month: September 🫧

These are all our special events, which run alongside our usual program of Essential and Social Sessions - 7 days a week.

We’ll keep this post pinned to the top of the page so you can revisit it whenever you need. For more details on the acts, head to the description on the schedule via the app or website!

An keep an eye out on stories each week for a sample of what’s in store 💜

Lonely in London? Sauna as the new place to socialise... 🌀

London can be such a fun and busy city. But, despite being surrounded by so many people, us Londoners are feeling increasingly isolated.

Many of us are working from home. Typical social spaces revolve around alcohol and aren’t designed to help you meet new people. So, we’ve built a new kind of space...

When we opened last Autumn, we were chasing a dream we couldn’t quite find anywhere else.

A place to connect with people, listen to amazing music, and leave feeling really (really) good. All without the pressure to consume alcohol o

When we opened our shutters in August 2024, it wasn’t just about building a business. It was about building the kind of Social Club we wished existed in London 🫧

So much of social life here is often centred around alcohol, with pubs and clubs the default for meeting friends or hearing new music. Our question was: what if you put sauna and ice bathing in its place? Instead of waking up with a hangover, you wake up feeling healthy and well-rested?

That spark of an idea became Sauna Social Club. A space for music, creativity and connection. A place where you might find yourself meditating to m

Meet the Team: Maze ✨

Maze joined the team a few months ago and is almost certainly everyone’s favourite 💜

From the dance floor to a sauna sweep, maze has it all under control! Their favourite bit of the new space is our gorgeous drench shower, if you haven’t yet, try it out! It really is as good as they say 🫧

Cosy season is just around the corner ✨

So many SSC members tell us how much or a whirlwind this summer has been, and we agree! 

Think we’re all looking forward to slowing down, reflecting, feeling cosy wrapped in a blanket, Sunday roasts followed by a nap, and spending lots of hours whiling the day away with a book in the tea loft 💜

These are the days we love the most, that post sauna high, that has you nodding off immediately. Perfection 🫧

Prest is a mountain above Aurland, overlooking the Aurlandsfjord.

Saunasaari was built for one thing: sauna.
Around the turn of the millennium, the City of Helsinki decided this little island – then called Pikkusaari – should become a sauna village. So they went looking for someone to build it. That someone was Rainer Hanhilahti, who knew a thing or two about tourism and traditional log building. Back then, the island had three saunas: Perinnesavu, Haapasavu and Pihasavu.
